articles.title: Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja, Pat Cummins claims explained as 2018 ball-tampering scandal rocks Australian cricket again
articles.summary: What was 'sandpapergate', who was involved and what were the punishments? Ball-tampering scandal is back in focus following Usman Khawaja’s claims that the entire team knew about the illegal methods being used; Pat Cummins has denied his claims as "100 per cent wrong"
articles.body:
Australia's enthralling 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa in October marked the Baggy Greens' first tour of the country since the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The controversy saw Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft handed lengthy bans after Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

The 2026 series, though, was free from toxicity around 'sandpapergate' and looked to have finally moved the conversation on from the infamous incident at Newlands just under a decade ago.

But, sensationally, former Aussie opener Usman Khawaja has now reignited discussion with the explosive claims in his new book 'Sabr' that the entire team were part of a plot to use illegal methods to elicit reverse swing.

These are claims that Warner has supported, but Australia's bowling group, led by current Test captain Pat Cummins, has firmly denied.

After the initial scandal, Khawaja's revelations, and Cummins' 68-minute press conference on Friday in response , Sky Sports takes you through everything you need to know as one of the biggest cricket stories takes yet another turn...

That was the name given to the March 2018 ball-tampering scandal during Australia's Test tour of South Africa after Bancroft was caught on camera trying to rough up one side of the ball with sandpaper in order the make it swing through the air.

The incident occurred on day three of the third Test in Cape Town while South Africa were batting in their second innings, with Bancroft aiming to hide the sandpaper, which he initially said was a piece of tape, in his trousers after realising he had been spotted.

At the close of play, Bancroft and Australia captain Smith admitted to ball-tampering during a press conference, although neither initially disclosed the use of sandpaper. Smith revealed that the plan had been devised by the team's 'leadership group' during the lunch break.

Smith and vice-captain Warner stood down from their leadership roles for the remainder of the Cape Town Test but remained in the side, with Tim Paine taking over as captain. The Baggy Greens subsequently slumped to a crushing 322-run defeat, being bowled out for just 107 in their second innings. Warner top-scored with 32, Bancroft made 26 and Smith managed just seven.

Smith, Warner and Bancroft were sent home ahead of the fourth Test, in which Australia were hammered by 492 runs to fall to a 3-1 series defeat, and later received hefty bans from international and domestic cricket, ranging from nine months to a year.

They were each found by Cricket Australia to have engaged in conduct against the spirit of the game and harmful to its interests.

Warner was found to have led the plot to alter the condition of the ball, including guiding Bancroft on how to use the sandpaper.

Warner was handed a 12-month ban and told he would never again be considered for a leadership position within the Australian team.

Smith, who was eventually succeeded permanently by Paine as captain, also received a 12-month suspension for failing to prevent a plan he knew about and making misleading comments in the aftermath. He was further barred from holding a leadership role until at least 12 months after the conclusion of his ban.

Bancroft, meanwhile, was handed a nine-month suspension.

Australia's bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon escaped punishment, later issuing a joint statement in 2021 insisting they had no prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plot.

Khawaja reignited the controversy surrounding sandpapergate in November with explosive claims that the entire Australian team knew sandpaper was being used to alter the ball. His allegations directly contradicted previous statements from Cricket Australia and members of the bowling attack, which maintained that only Smith, Bancroft and Warner were involved in the plot.

The batter, who retired from international cricket following Australia's 4-1 Ashes victory to England last winter, said: "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us."

In further extracts from his autobiography, released on Saturday, Khawaja alleged that discussions about ball-tampering had been held "openly and lightheartedly" across the entire squad, involving not just the batters, bowlers and coaching staff but the wider team. He also claimed he was never questioned as part of Cricket Australia's internal investigation into the scandal.

He also added that he had chosen to speak about the sandpapergate scandal now after promising childhood friend Warner that ​he would share his side of the story - claims that Warner has backed as "100 per cent accurate" in the days since the book's release.

Australia's current Test captain, Cummins, who was a relatively inexperienced member of the side at the time, playing just his 13th Test when the scandal unfolded, rejected Khawaja's latest allegations on Friday.

He opened the press conference by insisting he was prepared to answer questions for as long as necessary, making clear he did not want the controversy repeatedly dragged back into the spotlight every time a new book was published or fresh claims emerged.

After an hour, a cricket administrator suggested bringing the press conference to a close, but Cummins once again invited reporters to continue asking questions for as long as they wished. The session eventually lasted another 10 minutes.

"When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, ​he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," ‌Cummins told reporters.

"I did not know that was happening, but Usman actually says things that ​are actually far more serious than that.

"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."

Cummins, who was appointed Australia captain in November 2021, criticised Khawaja for being "casual" with the lives of his former team-mates and Australian cricket as a whole.

"Usman's a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and ​reputations," Cummins said.

"In his book, Ussie has been casual with my life and the ​lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket."

Arguably the most impactful claims made in support of Khawaja's revelations have been those of Warner, who has thrown his full backing behind his former team-mate.

"This is Usman's story. This is what Usman believes. Uzzy wrote down every single thing from that day on. Uzzy, thank you," Warner said.

"Now, this whole interview process was rushed and botched. Uzzy was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft. Uzzy was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me.

"We're not here to point fingers and we're not opening old wounds. It's about accountability, transparency and ensuring that the truth is properly examined."

"This is for everyone in Australia," he continued. "It's been the question that everyone's been asking. Uzzy, you said it how it is. It's 100 per cent accurate."

Warner reiterated his support of Khawaja after Cummins' press conference, saying that he feels that the Aussie captain "threw Uzzy under the bus."

Former Australia bowler Chadd Sayers, who was part of the 2018 tour of South Africa, has also claimed that "everything Usman said was accurate."

Alongside Cummins, bowler Starc has denied any prior knowledge of sandpapergate, backing the joint statement released by the bowlers five years ago.

"There are differing opinions of eight years ago," Starc said. "We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.

"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but from where I stand my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021."

Australia opener Nic Maddinson was not shy to share his displeasure with the fact that the scandal had reappeared in the headlines when speaking to 10 Sport .

"It's obviously disappointing that it keeps coming up," Maddinson added.

"But it's that time of year, isn't it? Christmas comes along and people have books to sell. Things come out. It's just disappointing."

Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who was not part of the governing board at the time of the scandal, has ruled out a fresh inquiry into the incident in the wake of Khawaja's claims.

Greenberg told Australian radio station SEN : "We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman. Our position hasn't changed on that."

Finally, is there anything more still to come out?

While Cricket Australia's investigation concluded that Warner, Smith and Bancroft were the only players involved in the ball-tampering plot, Bancroft suggested otherwise in a 2021 interview, saying it was "self-explanatory" that the bowlers in the team must have been aware the ball was being tampered with. He has, however, declined to comment on the matter since the publication of Khawaja's book.

Cricket Australia has previously indicated it would be open to investigating any fresh information that came to light, but, according to Greenberg, Khawaja's claims have not met the threshold for reopening the inquiry.

Eight years after the scandal first rocked Australian cricket, the latest revelations have added yet another chapter to a controversy that refuses to go away.

And with so many questions still being raised, it remains to be seen whether this is the last we hear of sandpapergate.

articles.title: 6/24 on debut! Mahli Beardman rips through England as Australia take 1-0 lead
articles.summary: Debutant Mahli Beardman produced a sensational performance with the ball, claiming 6/24 to power Australia to a comfortable seven-wicket victory over
articles.body: Debutant Mahli Beardman produced a sensational performance with the ball, claiming 6/24 to power Australia to a comfortable seven-wicket victory over England in the first ODI in Perth on Friday.England's batting line-up crumbled for just 131 in 33.4 overs after Australia elected to bowl. The hosts made light work of the chase, getting to 132/3 in 23.3 overs, with captain Mitch Marsh leading the charge through a blistering half-century.For Beardman, the dream debut was an occasion to cherish."It's just a great privilege and honour to be able to represent my country, and then to be able to go out and take a few wickets as well is just a cherry on top," he said.The contest, however, unfolded amid fresh tensions in Australian cricket following the publication of Usman Khawaja's autobiography this week. The former Australia batter claimed that knowledge of the 2018 ball-tampering episode in Cape Town was not limited to the players who were eventually punished.Current Test captain Pat Cummins strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as "100% wrong" during an hour-long press conference on Friday. David Warner, meanwhile, backed Khawaja's version while on television commentary. Warner himself had received a 12-month playing ban for his involvement in the scandal.On the field, Australia's fast bowlers made early inroads on a lively Perth Stadium surface. Spencer Johnson (3/42) and Xavier Bartlett (1/46) accounted for openers Ben Duckett, who scored nine, and Tom Banton, who managed 25.Beardman then took centre stage, dismantling England's middle and lower order with a superb display of seam bowling. The Western Australia pacer consistently hit the right lengths and extracted movement off the pitch, making life difficult for the visitors.Wicketkeeper Josh Inglis held catches to dismiss England captain Harry Brook for one, Joe Root for 17 and Jordan Cox for two, all falling to the 21-year-old right-arm quick.Sam Curran and Liam Dawson departed without troubling the scorers as Beardman became the first Australian since Tony Dodemaide in 1988 to claim five wickets on ODI debut.He was not finished yet. Beardman completed his six-wicket haul by having Jofra Archer caught at gully for 11. Gus Atkinson, England's highest scorer with an unbeaten 29, was left stranded as the innings folded.England briefly threatened to make the chase interesting when Atkinson bowled Travis Head for a golden duck in the second over. However, Marsh quickly took control, smashing four sixes on his way to a rapid fifty before Jamie Overton (1/35) dismissed him in the deep.Archer then removed Cooper Connolly for 27, but England had little left to offer. Matt Renshaw joined Inglis at the crease, and the pair completed the chase without further damage.The victory gives Australia a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series. The second match will be played in Adelaide on Sunday, with the final game scheduled in Hobart on Wednesday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Most ducks in ODIs: Virat Kohli equals Sachin Tendulkar's unwanted India record
articles.summary: Virat Kohli on Friday matched one of the unwanted record of batting legend Sachin Tendulkar.
articles.body: Virat Kohli on Friday matched one of the unwanted record of batting legend Sachin Tendulkar. Kohli was dismissed for a four-ball duck as India suffered a 244-run defeat against New Zealand in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui.With the dismissal, Kohli's tally of ducks in ODI cricket moved to 20, taking him level with Tendulkar for the most ducks by an Indian batter in the format. However, Kohli reached the mark in 321 matches, while Tendulkar took 463 matches to register the same number.Former India pacer Javagal Srinath is third on the list with 19 ducks, while Anil Kumble and Rohit Sharma have 18 each. Rohit also endured a difficult outing on Friday, departing for a golden duck during India's chase.It was a day to forget for the Indian batting line-up as Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson made full use of the conditions to bowl out the visitors for just 89 while defending a target of 334.Earlier, Will Young scored a century and Henry picked up six wickets to help New Zealand register a 244-run victory. The win keeps the hosts in contention to draw the five-match series, although they can no longer win it.India lead the series 2-1, with the third ODI having been abandoned due to rain. The final match will be played at the same venue on Sunday.India's chase got off to a disastrous start as Henry struck three times in the opening over, dismissing Rohit, Kohli and Shreyas Iyer without allowing the visitors to get on the scoreboard. India were reduced to 0/3 before Ruturaj Gaikwad also departed.Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel then put together a 44-run partnership, scoring 27 and 21 respectively, while Naman Dhir added a quickfire 21. Their efforts helped India avoid their biggest defeat in ODI cricket by runs, but the visitors were eventually bowled out for 89.India's heaviest defeat in terms of runs remains their 245-run loss to Sri Lanka in 2000. Henry claimed three more wickets after his opening-over burst to finish with six as New Zealand bowled India out for their sixth-lowest total in ODI cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mahli Beardman and Matt Henry replicate rare ODI feat last achieved by Rashid Khan and Paul Stirling in 2017
articles.summary: Friday, November 13, turned into a memorable day for fast bowlers as Australia's Mahli Beardman and New Zealand's Matt Henry produced sensational
articles.body: Friday, November 13, turned into a memorable day for fast bowlers as Australia's Mahli Beardman and New Zealand's Matt Henry produced sensational six-wicket hauls in separate ODI matches.Beardman announced himself on the international stage with figures of 6/24 against England in Perth, while Henry delivered a match-winning spell of 6/27 to help New Zealand thrash India by 244 runs at Mount Maunganui.The two performances marked only the second instance of two six-wicket hauls being recorded in ODI cricket on the same day. The previous occasion came on March 17, 2017, when Ireland's Paul Stirling and Afghanistan's Rashid Khan both claimed six wickets in the same ODI at Greater Noida.Mahli Beardman demolishes England on ODI debutThe 21-year-old Beardman enjoyed a dream start to his international career, ripping through England's batting line-up in the first ODI at Perth Stadium. England were bowled out for 131 in 33.4 overs after Beardman returned remarkable figures of 6/24. The Australian pacer removed Harry Brook and Joe Root early before running through the middle and lower order to complete a memorable debut performance.His spell triggered England's collapse from 38/2 to 60/7, leaving the visitors struggling to put up a competitive total. Spencer Johnson also chipped in with three wickets as Australia dominated with the ball. In reply, Australia chased down the target in 23.3 overs, reaching 132/3 to register a comfortable seven-wicket victory and take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.Beardman's figures were the fourth-best by a bowler on ODI debut, underlining the significance of his performance. He also became the first Australian since Tony Dodemaide in 1988 to claim a five-wicket haul on his ODI debut.Matt Henry destroys India as New Zealand register massive winWhile Beardman stole the spotlight in Perth, Henry produced an equally devastating performance in New Zealand's fourth ODI against India at Bay Oval.After New Zealand posted 333/8 in their 50 overs, courtesy of Will Young's brilliant 125 off 108 deliveries, Henry dismantled India's batting order with a career-best ODI spell of 6/27.The right-arm pacer made an immediate impact, dismissing Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer in the opening over to leave India reeling at 0/3. India never recovered from the early damage and were eventually bowled out for just 89 in 26.4 overs, suffering a crushing 244-run defeat. Henry was supported by Matthew Fisher, who picked up three wickets.The victory kept New Zealand alive in the five-match series, with India retaining a 2-1 lead ahead of the final ODI.Rashid Khan and Paul Stirling's historic feat in 2017The previous instance of two six-wicket hauls on the same day came during the second ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland at Greater Noida on March 17, 2017. Batting first, Afghanistan posted a formidable 338, powered by captain Asghar Stanikzai's century. Ireland's Paul Stirling produced a remarkable bowling performance, claiming 6/55 to restrict Afghanistan after they had threatened to cross 350.In response, Afghanistan leg-spinner Rashid Khan returned figures of 6/43 to derail Ireland's chase. Stirling, who had also scored 95 with the bat, was among his victims as Ireland were dismissed for 304, handing Afghanistan a 34-run victory.Both Stirling and Rashid recorded career-best ODI bowling figures at the time, making it a landmark match in the format's history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India's Virat Kohli one of three players out for ducks in ODI loss as New Zealand's Matt Henry takes triple-wicket-maiden in first over
articles.summary: Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer all fall for nought as India reduced to 0-3 and then bundled out for 89 chasing 334 against New Zealand; Black Caps' 244-run victory keeps five-match series alive heading into Sunday's finale at Mount Maunganui; teams will then play two Tests
articles.body:
Chasing 334 in Mount Maunganui to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, India's reply got off to a dreadful start when seamer Henry's first delivery squared up Rohit and induced an edge to Finn Allen in the slip cordon.

Kohli survived the next three balls, although the first whistled past his outside edge, only to then be bowled by a nip-backer that kept low from the fifth delivery of Henry's over.

The Kiwi bowler, who earned his best ODI figures of 6-27, then trapped India captain Shreyas lbw with the final ball of the over, to set India on their way to their second-heaviest ODI defeat, after the 245-run drubbing by Sri Lanka in Sharjah in October 2000.

Henry was unable to complete a hat-trick with Ishan Kishan seeing off the first delivery of the 34-year-old's second over - another nip-backer which rattled Kishan on the thigh pad, too high for a genuine lbw appeal - but he went on to bowl the same batter for 27 in the 21st over when the left-hander inside-edged onto his leg stump.

Henry also castled tailenders Kuldeep Yadav and Gurnoor Brar as India were bundled out for their sixth-lowest ODI total, going down in just 26.4 overs at Bay Oval.

The bowler said: "With the way the wind was going, I wasn't too worried about the swing. From ball one it was just about trying to bring the stumps in play, really.

"We knew that there was a small window there with the new ball that you could put the ‌batters under pressure, so it's just trying to be as simple as possible.

"When it moves sharply like that in the first over, when people are facing first balls, it's pretty tough."

Earlier, Will Young top-scored for the Black Caps in their 333 all out with 125 from 108 balls, having been dropped on five twice in as many balls off the bowling of Auqib Nabi, first by Rohit at slip and then by wicketkeeper Kishan.

New Zealand - who lost the preceding T20I series 3-2 - will now look to square the ODI series at Mount Maunganui on Sunday, after suffering defeats in Auckland and Wellington and then seeing the third match in Hamilton washed out.

The Kiwis will then host India in two Tests, starting in Wellington on November 19 ahead of a second fixture in Christchurch from November 27.

articles.title: Deepti Sharma bags second ICC Player of the Month award; Marco Jansen claims men's honour
articles.summary: South Africa's Marco Jansen and India's Deepti Sharma have been rewarded for their all-round brilliance, winning the ICC Men's and Women's Player of the
articles.body: South Africa's Marco Jansen and India's Deepti Sharma have been rewarded for their all-round brilliance, winning the ICC Men's and Women's Player of the Month awards for October. While Jansen dominated with both bat and ball during South Africa's high-profile Test series against Australia, Deepti played a crucial role in India's commanding white-ball sweep of Zimbabwe.Jansen's match-winning contributions helped him climb to the top of two ICC Test Player Rankings categories, while Deepti showcased her versatility with impactful performances in both the ODI and T20I formats. The award marks the second time the Indian all-rounder has received the women's honour, having previously won it in December 2023.Marco Jansen's all-round brilliance against AustraliaJansen enjoyed an impressive month, scoring 198 runs and claiming 13 wickets with his left-arm pace bowling. His standout performance came in the second Test of the three-match ICC World Test Championship series against Australia in Gqeberha.The 26-year-old played a crucial role with the bat, scoring 85 runs before producing match figures of five for 33 and one for 34 to help South Africa secure a memorable victory.His performances also propelled him to the top of the ICC Test Bowling and All-rounder Rankings. Jansen became the first South African bowler to occupy the No. 1 position since Kagiso Rabada in 2024 and the first player from the country to top the Test all-rounders' rankings since Vernon Philander in August 2014.Jansen won the men's award ahead of Pakistan's Arafat Minhas and West Indies captain Shai Hope, who were also shortlisted for their performances during October.Deepti Sharma shines in India's white-ball sweep of ZimbabweDeepti earned the women's award after delivering impactful performances with both bat and ball during India's home series against Zimbabwe. In the ICC Women's Championship ODI series, the Indian all-rounder scored an unbeaten 106 in her only batting opportunity and picked up five wickets at an economy rate of 3.42 as India completed a dominant 3-0 series sweep.She carried her form into the T20I series, scoring 49 off 37 deliveries in her only innings and adding two wickets with her off-spin bowling.The latest recognition marks Deepti's second ICC Women's Player of the Month award, following her maiden honour in December 2023. She finished ahead of Bangladesh's Sobhana Mostary and Australia's Annabel Sutherland, who were also shortlisted.Speaking after receiving the award, Deepti expressed happiness over India's performance and highlighted her century as a particularly special moment."I'm pleased to win the ICC Women's Player of the Month award. The series against Zimbabwe was a great one for us, and I'm proud of the way the team performed, especially the youngsters. Scoring a century was a particularly special moment for me, made even more meaningful as it contributed to a winning cause," she said.Deepti also thanked the voting panel, fans, teammates and coaches for their support, dedicating the award to her supporters across the world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli's special gesture for Matt Henry goes viral after New Zealand pacer's six-wicket demolition of India
articles.summary: Virat Kohli displayed a fine example of sportsmanship despite India's crushing defeat against New Zealand in the fourth ODI, presenting pacer Matt Henry
articles.body: Virat Kohli displayed a fine example of sportsmanship despite India's crushing defeat against New Zealand in the fourth ODI, presenting pacer Matt Henry with an Indian team jersey following his match-winning performance in the contest on Friday.A video shared by the official Instagram handle of the Blackcaps captured the interaction between the two cricketers after the match. Kohli was seen exchanging a few words with Henry before gifting the New Zealand pacer an Indian jersey, acknowledging his outstanding contribution to the visitors' 244-run victory.Henry had delivered a devastating spell, returning career-best figures of 6/27 to dismantle India's batting line-up. Chasing New Zealand's 334-run target, the hosts were bowled out for just 89 in 26.4 overs, suffering one of their heaviest defeats in ODI cricket.The right-arm pacer made an immediate impact, removing Rohit Sharma, Kohli and stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer for ducks in the opening over itself. The three early dismissals left India reeling and brought back memories of the 2019 World Cup semifinal, when New Zealand had similarly derailed India's campaign.Interestingly, Kohli has managed 59 runs off 60 deliveries against Henry in ODIs, striking at 98.33. The New Zealand quick has dismissed the Indian batting great three times in the format.Henry's performance also added to his growing record against India. He has now taken four or more wickets against the Men in Blue on four occasions in just 12 ODI innings, the joint-most such instances by a bowler.The six-wicket haul also took him level with Shane Bond for the third-highest number of five-wicket hauls by a New Zealand bowler in ODIs. Richard Hadlee, with five, and Trent Boult, with six, are ahead of the duo.Earlier in the match, Will Young played a pivotal role in New Zealand's imposing total of 333. The right-hander struck a superb 125 off 108 balls, including 14 fours and four sixes, after receiving two early reprieves.Young initially added 85 runs with opener Tim Seifert, who contributed 58 off 48 deliveries with six fours and three sixes. Following Seifert's dismissal and a brief middle-order slowdown, Young combined with Finn Allen for another important 90-run partnership. Allen scored 41 off 30 balls, hitting five fours and two sixes.New Zealand received further contributions from Mitchell Santner (24), Kristian Clarke (22) and Kyle Jamieson (19 not out) to push their total beyond the 300-run mark. For India, Axar Patel, Auqib Nabi and Gurnoor Brar picked up two wickets apiece.India's response never recovered from Henry's opening burst. Ishan Kishan top-scored with 27, while Axar Patel and Naman Dhir managed 21 each. The rest of the batting line-up failed to offer meaningful resistance as India folded for 89.Despite the comprehensive defeat, India continue to lead the five-match ODI series 2-1, with the final match set to determine the outcome.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'World Cup is the bigger picture': Harry Brook reacts after England's crushing defeat against Australia
articles.summary: Australia's pace attack gave England a reality check in the opening ODI in Perth, with debutant Mahli Beardman stealing the spotlight through a
articles.body: Australia's pace attack gave England a reality check in the opening ODI in Perth, with debutant Mahli Beardman stealing the spotlight through a sensational six-wicket haul. England captain Harry Brook acknowledged the youngster's outstanding performance after the visitors were bowled out for 131 and suffered a seven-wicket defeat at Optus Stadium.Beardman returned figures of 6/24 in 7.4 overs, becoming the first Australian since Tony Dodemaide in 1988 to claim a five-wicket haul on his ODI debut. His performance helped Australia take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series, leaving England with plenty to address before the second match in Adelaide.Speaking after the defeat, Brook praised the young Australian pacer for exploiting the conditions and consistently hitting the right areas."Yeah. We've been here for a week and a half or so. We've prepared extremely well. Australia have bowled extremely well. Mahli Beardman was outstanding today. He put the ball in the right areas, got enough out of the surface to dismiss us, and, yeah, they put in a good performance with the ball," Brook said.England's batting collapse in PerthAfter Australia won the toss and elected to bowl, England struggled to cope with the pace and bounce on offer. Tom Banton top-scored with 25, while Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson also contributed 25 and an unbeaten 29 respectively.However, Beardman's relentless spell triggered a collapse that saw England slip from 38/2 to 60/7. He removed Brook, Joe Root, Jordan Cox, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson and Jofra Archer to record the best ODI debut bowling figures by an Australian.Spencer Johnson provided further support with three wickets as England were dismissed for 131 in 33.4 overs.Australia made light work of the chase, reaching 132/3 in just 23.3 overs. Captain Mitchell Marsh led from the front with a blistering 50 off 30 deliveries, while Cooper Connolly scored 27 and Matt Renshaw remained unbeaten on 26. The hosts sealed a comfortable seven-wicket victory.Harry Brook admits England failed to adaptBrook admitted that England had discussed adapting their approach to different conditions but failed to execute their plans against Australia's disciplined bowling attack."We spoke a lot about adaptability. We want to adapt to different surfaces, and as I said before, we've been here for a week and a half."We prepared extremely well. We knew that certain shots weren't going to work on this pitch, but look, the Australian attack bowled extremely well. They put the ball in the right areas for 30-odd overs, and we probably didn't execute our skill well enough," he added.2027 ODI World Cup remains the bigger pictureWith the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa approaching, Brook said these challenging conditions and experiences would be important for England's preparations. He also insisted that his side remained confident of bouncing back despite losing the opening match."Definitely, and that is the bigger picture (World Cup preparations). We've got a World Cup in South Africa in 12 months' time, and these experiences, we take them, we learn from them as much as we possibly can. We're not out of this series yet. We've been in this position a couple of times before and managed to bounce back. So hopefully we can do that when we get to Adelaide," he said.England will now look to level the series in the second ODI in Adelaide before the teams head to Hobart for the final match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Saqib Khan's dream Test debut goes in vain as rain forces Pakistan-Sri Lanka opener into a draw
articles.summary: Debutant Saqib Khan produced a memorable seven-wicket haul, but persistent rain and bad light denied Pakistan and Sri Lanka a result in the opening Test
articles.body: Debutant Saqib Khan produced a memorable seven-wicket haul, but persistent rain and bad light denied Pakistan and Sri Lanka a result in the opening Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday.Sri Lanka secured a narrow 12-run first-innings lead after scoring 446 in response to Pakistan's 434/9 declared. The hosts then reached 284/8 in their second innings before both teams settled for a draw, with weather interruptions playing a major role throughout the contest.Dhananjaya de Silva, Kusal Mendis put Sri Lanka aheadPakistan, after opting to bat first, posted 434/9 declared, with Saud Shakeel leading the scoring with 93. Mohammad Tayyab Arif contributed 57, while Arafat Minhas and Babar Azam also registered half-centuries.In reply, Sri Lanka recovered from early setbacks through a magnificent fifth-wicket partnership between Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis.De Silva scored 167 off 246 deliveries, hitting 20 boundaries, while Mendis contributed 119 from 202 balls, including 10 fours and four sixes.Their partnership took Sri Lanka past the 400-run mark and put the visitors in a strong position. However, Pakistan's bowlers struck back to restrict them to 446, giving the hosts a slender 12-run lead.Saqib Khan shines with seven-wicket haul on debutSaqib Khan emerged as Pakistan's biggest positive from the contest, delivering an outstanding performance with the ball on his Test debut. The 31-year-old dismissed De Silva early on the fourth morning before removing Mendis shortly afterwards. He continued to trouble the Sri Lankan lower order and finished with figures of 7/130 in 34 overs.Sri Lanka lost their final six wickets for just 42 runs, allowing Pakistan to restrict the visitors' first-innings advantage.Saqib became only the fourth Pakistan bowler to claim a seven-wicket haul on Test debut, joining Mohammad Zahid, Mohammad Nazir and Abrar Ahmed.Saud Shakeel's 97 helps Pakistan fight backPakistan faced a challenging situation in their second innings but found resistance through Saud Shakeel. The left-hander scored 97, narrowly missing out on a century, as Pakistan recovered from 125/5 to reach 284/8.With time running out and weather continuing to interrupt play, the two teams eventually agreed to a draw, bringing an end to a closely fought opening Test.Second Test shifted to RawalpindiThe opening match was significantly affected by rain and bad light, with several sessions lost during the five days. The second and final Test, originally scheduled to be played in Lahore, has also been moved to Rawalpindi due to worsening smog conditions in Lahore. articles.title: 'Can't take any series for granted': Kagiso Rabada warns South Africa against complacency ahead of Bangladesh Tests
articles.summary: Fresh from dethroning Australia to become the world's top-ranked Test side, South Africa are determined to maintain their winning momentum as they prepare
articles.body: Fresh from dethroning Australia to become the world's top-ranked Test side, South Africa are determined to maintain their winning momentum as they prepare to host Bangladesh in a two-match Test series. However, fast bowler Kagiso Rabada has warned his teammates against complacency, insisting that the Proteas will not underestimate their opponents despite the difference in ICC rankings.The first Test is scheduled to begin at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg on Sunday, with South Africa looking to build on their impressive performances against Australia. Rabada believes Bangladesh will arrive with plenty of confidence and motivation, making the contest an exciting challenge for the hosts.Speaking at a press conference on Friday, the South African pacer stressed that no international series could be taken lightly."In international cricket, you can't take any series for granted. There are always high stakes on every game that you play. And moving into this series against Bangladesh, they'll be heightened in their spirits, looking at the way they've played in recent times," Rabada said.Rabada excited about Bangladesh challengeAlthough Bangladesh are ranked eighth in the latest ICC Test rankings, Rabada believes their recent performances make them a dangerous opponent. The visitors have developed a competitive bowling attack and will be keen to make their mark against the reigning top-ranked Test side.Bangladesh also recorded a historic nine-wicket Test victory in Australia in August, further strengthening their belief ahead of the South Africa tour.Rabada welcomed the challenge, saying that competing against quality opposition was exactly what international cricket was about."It's actually exciting, you know? You want to be up against the best opposition that you can be. And I think they'd want to come here and prove a point and I'm really looking forward to this battle. I think it will show how healthy cricket is," he added.South Africa wary of complacencyRabada, who became the fastest bowler to reach 350 Test wickets during the Australia series, also admitted that South Africa had previously underestimated opponents and paid the price.The experienced pacer said the team would be mindful of avoiding a similar situation against Bangladesh and would look to maintain the intensity that has brought them success over the last two years."I think it's human nature, we've found ourselves on that side before where we probably got a bit too complacent. It's something that we have to guard against, to really give it our best shot and not drop the intensity, to keep our standards right up there," he said.The 30-year-old further emphasised that South Africa's focus would remain on their approach rather than the final result, with the team determined to continue playing an aggressive brand of cricket."We're not really thinking about the result, we're just going to think about how we want to play, because that's what we've been doing these past two years, having that desperation to win. And yeah, getting into the faces of our opponents, that's exactly how we want to play. We'll be looking to do more of the same," Rabada concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Sandpapergate 'burning out of control'? How Australian media reacted to Pat Cummins news conference
articles.summary: The Australian newpapers have their say after Pat Cummins' extraordinary 68-minute news conference.
articles.body:
Eight years after cricket was rocked by the scandal which became known as "Sandpapergate", the controversy has been reignited.

Former batter Usman Khawaja released his autobiography in which he said the entire Australia team knew about the scheme and should have taken responsibility.

Captain Pat Cummins hit back in a news conference on Friday, saying Khawaja's claims were "100% wrong" and "nonsense".

That news conference lasted for over an hour at the end of a week which has reopened old wounds and pitted former team-mates against each other.

Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for tampering with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.

Khawaja has been supported by Warner and Chadd Sayers, a seam bowler who was part of the Australia squad on the 2018 tour of South Africa.

But Darren Lehmann - who was then the head coach - is among those to have rejected Khawaja's accusations, as are the former England batter Graeme Hick, who was one of his assistants, and Mitchell Starc, another bowler on the tour.

In Khawaja's book, published this week, he alleges Australia were urged to find ways to get the ball to swing by a coach and that Bancroft was later encouraged to cheat.

The fallout from Khawaja's autobiography has caused divides across Australian sport.

Here is how the Australian newspapers on Saturday have reacted to the latest chapter - Cummins' extraordinary news conference.

articles.title: 'Frequent collapses in seamer-friendly conditions are concerning': Gautam Gambhir identifies India's big batting problem
articles.summary: Gautam Gambhir is worried, and understandably so.
articles.body: Gautam Gambhir is worried, and understandably so. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa firmly in the team's sights, India's inability to cope with seamer-friendly, bouncy conditions is becoming an increasingly difficult problem to ignore.Being bowled out for 89 against New Zealand in the fourth ODI was bad enough. But Gambhir's concerns stretch beyond Friday's humiliation. India had also slipped to 111 for 7 in the second ODI while chasing a modest 135, eventually scraping home through the DLS method. Two batting collapses in conditions that offer a glimpse of what could await them in South Africa should set alarm bells ringing."There's no benefit to sweeping it under the carpet. It isn't just this match. Even in the previous match, we were seven down for 111 or 112. Today we lost, so we are talking about it," the India head coach said at the post-match press conference. "It's concerning because yes, there is some help here for the bowlers, so we have to be not only mentally but from the skill point of view we need to be ready as well. You aren't going to score 70-80 in the first 10 overs in these conditions. If you're 35-40 for no loss, that is also good enough. In India, the easiest time for batting is the first 10-15 overs. Here it's probably the hardest time. This is the difference in these conditions, and with the amount of experience we have, hopefully we can adapt in the last game."The India coach was particularly concerned about how quickly his team folded, rather than merely the final score. "You are always concerned when you get bundled out for 90-odd, why won't I be concerned? These are conditions which are going to be closest to what we might get during the World Cup," Gambhir said. "For me, the bigger concern is not the runs, it's how quickly we got bundled out, in around 26 or 27 overs. Hopefully, we can try and rectify that as soon as possible."The wobble-seam ball was a key weapon for wrecker-in-chief Matt Henry, but Gambhir was reluctant to make the wobble-seam delivery the centre of discussion and pinned the blame squarely on indecisive Indian footwork."Honestly, I don't go into this much technicality, wobble seam and all that. Ultimately, it is the job of the batsman to negate the movement whether it is the upright seam, wobble seam or scrambled seam," he said. "I thought more than the wobble seam, it's the areas that have probably created a problem for us. It was that length where you couldn't go forward, you couldn't go back. It was that half-half length. We had to be more committed towards it rather than getting stuck on the crease."The selection of Kuldeep Yadav ahead of Mohammed Siraj also raised eyebrows. Kuldeep endured a difficult outing, conceding 73 runs in eight wicketless overs. Gambhir defended the decision. "We thought that a wrist spinner would be more useful, as simple as it can get. In these conditions, especially on a bigger ground, if we can have a wrist spinner in the middle overs to try and take wickets, we thought that was an attacking option. Whatever we felt was the right combination, we went ahead with that."Kuldeep's lack of rhythm was another talking point, but Gambhir was not inclined to offer excuses on the basis of limited opportunities."Game time will always be limited as a spinner when you travel overseas. But whatever opportunities you get, you try and make the most of it. It's not that he hasn't got enough game time. He played three ODIs against West Indies at home in Oct. So, this debate about less game time, getting into rhythm doesn't hold for me," Gambhir said. "I think when you are playing international cricket, you should try and be in rhythm most of the time. And whatever opportunities you get, you should try and make the most of it."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Bring the stumps into play': Matt Henry reveals secret behind India's 89 all-out humiliation
articles.summary: Matt Henry on Friday at the Bay Oval reminded India why he remains their nemesis-in-chief.
articles.body: Matt Henry on Friday at the Bay Oval reminded India why he remains their nemesis-in-chief. A triple-wicket maiden in the opening over of the run chase accounted for Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer for ducks, laying the foundation for career-best ODI figures of 6 for 27 as India folded for 89 in a 244-run hammering. The plan for Henry was simple: stick to the basics and bring the stumps into play."With the way the wind was going, I wasn't too worried about getting swing. From ball one it was just about trying to bring the stumps into play. We knew there was a small window with the new ball to put the batters under pressure. When it moves sharply like that in the first over, facing the new ball for the top-order batters is pretty tough," Henry said.Reflecting on the extraordinary opening over, a modest Henry said he "just had a straightforward plan", but things fell neatly into place. "It's quite funny, isn't it? The wind was so strong and was pushing me a bit sideways. It was all about keeping things simple. It's funny when you just have a straightforward plan, a bit of luck as well — one shot a little bit low there too. So some good fortune as well."If Friday felt like deja vu for Indian fans, it was because Henry has made a habit of wrecking them on the biggest stages. From announcing himself on ODI debut in Wellington in Jan 2014 with 4 for 38 to his Player of the Match-winning performance of 3 for 37 in the 2019 World Cup semifinal at Old Trafford, Henry has consistently found India’s soft underbelly.He has troubled India in the Test arena too. Henry ripped through India's batting with 5/15 in the first innings of the Bengaluru Test in Oct 2024, helping bowl them out for 46 as New Zealand secured a historic 3-0 series sweep. He had also picked 5 for 42 against India in the 2025 Champions Trophy group stage in Dubai.Across formats and conditions, Henry has repeatedly found a way to expose India's batting vulnerabilities. Despite being one of India's most persistent tormentors, Henry played down his success against the team. "Oh, I don't want to get too carried away. They are a world-class outfit, and that's the message we know as a team competing against the Indian side. They have a lot of depth in their batting." Henry said. "They're leading 2-1, and we've got another game coming up soon. Hopefully we can level the series."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Matt Henry's three-ball demolition exposes India's batting frailties ahead of 2027 ODI World Cup
articles.summary: Three balls. That was all Matt Henry needed to turn India’s chase of 334 into a rout. Henry was only supposed to be passing through.
articles.body: Three balls. That was all Matt Henry needed to turn India’s chase of 334 into a rout.Henry was only supposed to be passing through. Having missed most of the T20Is with a leg injury and the early ODIs amid concussion concerns after colliding with Devon Conway, the seamer stayed back at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui simply to prove his fitness and get some overs into his legs before the Tests.Instead, he produced one of the most devastating opening overs in ODI cricket, reducing India to 0/3 and setting up a 244-run thrashing — India’s second-biggest defeat by runs in the format. India collapsed for 89 and the contest was effectively sealed before the visitors had even troubled the scorers.Henry’s first ball landed on a good length on off, kicked, and seamed away just enough to square up Rohit Sharma and kiss the outside edge on its way to first slip. It was a jarring sight, painfully reminiscent of the twilight of Rohit’s Test career and an increasingly familiar one when he faces quality fast bowling in overseas conditions.Next up was Virat Kohli. Henry pitched fuller, drew him forward and beat the outside edge by inches. Three balls later, he wobbled the seam from an identical spot. This one nipped back in, stayed low and rattled Kohli’s stumps.Then came Shreyas Iyer, walking out for his captaincy debut and walking back with a golden duck — the first Indian skipper to suffer that fate. Trapped on the crease by one that darted past his inside edge, Iyer fell to a DRS review while Henry was already mid-celebration. India’s first run came off the 17th delivery of the innings.For anyone watching, it was impossible not to be dragged back to Old Trafford in July 2019, when Henry’s 3/37 ripped the heart out of India’s World Cup semifinal chase. Seven years on, the scars remain wide open.With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa looming, where conditions could offer similar bounce and seam movement, this rout should set off alarm bells. A hint of lateral movement was all it took to expose India’s glaring technical chinks.To be fair, Henry was not operating in isolation. Kyle Jamieson used his height to extract extra bounce and movement, getting Ruturaj Gaikwad (5) to edge a feeble push outside off to second slip as India slipped to 9 for 4.Ishan Kishan (27 off 53) and Axar Patel (21 off 36) briefly resisted with a 44-run stand. Naman Dhir (21 off 24) muscled two sixes, but Matt Fisher (3 for 31) kept hitting hard lengths at high pace to snuff out any fight. Henry then returned to clean up the tail, finishing with career-best ODI figures.If India’s batting was brittle, the thinking off the field was equally baffling. On a surface offering genuine seam and bounce, leaving Mohammed Siraj out of the XI again defied cricketing logic. Gautam Gambhir’s selection calls continue to puzzle, raising serious questions about the roadmap ahead.Cruelly for India, they had walked into the innings break believing they held the momentum. After Tim Seifert (58 off 48) and Will Young forged an 85-run opening stand, Young took over and ensured there was no let-up.Dropped twice on 5 off Auqib Nabi in the second over of New Zealand’s innings, Young cashed in with a career-best 125 off 108 balls. Alongside Finn Allen (41 off 30), he took down Kuldeep Yadav (0 for 73 in 8 overs) in a 90-run fourth-wicket stand before Rohit redeemed an earlier dropped chance with a sharp diving catch at short cover. Part-timer Naman Dhir then removed Young and took a diving catch to dismiss Michael Bracewell off Gurnoor Brar. Axar (2 for 39) and Arshdeep Singh, who removed Mitchell Santner, helped India take 6 for 77 in the final 13.1 overs and bowl New Zealand out for 333.New Zealand, trailing 2-1, now head into Sunday’s final ODI without Henry and Jamieson, both bound for Test duty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 141 overs lost: Babar Azam, Mike Hesson suggest 'pink' solution for Pakistan's winter Test problem
articles.summary: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has called for the use of the pink ball in day Test matches at home to be seriously considered after rain and poor light
articles.body: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has called for the use of the pink ball in day Test matches at home to be seriously considered after rain and poor light disrupted the opening Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, which ended in a draw with nearly 141 overs lost.Hesson and Pakistan captain Babar Azam are open to the idea of using the pink ball in future home Test series, particularly during the winter months when weather conditions make it difficult to complete scheduled playing hours.The opening Test was repeatedly interrupted by bad light, forcing players to leave the field before the scheduled close of play on most days. The fourth day was called off during the afternoon session because of rain.Even before the rain arrived on the fourth day, umpires had to suspend play because the light had deteriorated to a level where continuing with the red ball under lights could have put players at risk of injury.The match was already heading towards a draw when play resumed on the fifth day. Pakistan were leading by just 45 runs with one wicket down as they looked to build a target for Sri Lanka.Pakistan ended up batting through the day before play was called off at 4:18 pm, almost two hours before the scheduled close at 6:10 pm. The decision came after Saud Shakeel was dismissed in the 90s for the second time in the match.The first three days had also seen significant interruptions, with only 14.2, 15.1 and 12 overs bowled in the evening sessions respectively.The International Cricket Council (ICC), following its last quarterly meeting, has approved the use of pink balls in day Tests as an option to address the problem of overs being lost due to bad light. Hesson believes Pakistan should consider the option for future home series."It is certainly something that needs to be talked about for the future series," Hesson told the host broadcaster after the match. "It is going to be a challenge to play Test matches in this time of the year regardless of where in Pakistan. As the ICC have now allowed that to be an option, this is something that seriously needs to be considered before the series."Babar, however, pointed out that the short gap between the two Tests would not have given Pakistan enough time to prepare for a pink-ball match. With only three days between the two games, he said players needed more time to get used to the different conditions and behaviour of the pink ball."You will need to prepare for it as we usually play with the red ball," he said in the post-match presentation. "A couple of days are not enough to prepare to play a Test with the pink ball. It is a good that we have it as an option, but the preparation for a pink ball Test demands more time."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Just sixth overall and first-ever in Pakistan's history: Saud Shakeel joins rare Test batting record list which includes Mahela Jayawardene and Gordon Greenidge
articles.summary: Saud Shakeel came agonisingly close to scoring a century for the second time in the same Test but his 97-run knock helped Pakistan hold off Sri Lanka and
articles.body: Saud Shakeel came agonisingly close to scoring a century for the second time in the same Test but his 97-run knock helped Pakistan hold off Sri Lanka and secure a draw in the opening match of the series in Rawalpindi on Friday.Shakeel, who had scored 93 in Pakistan's first innings total of 434/9 declared, fell just three runs short of his century in the second innings. The left-hander spent most of the fifth and final day at the crease before Lahiru Kumara bowled him after he had faced 210 deliveries.By the time Shakeel was dismissed, Pakistan had reached 284/8, taking their overall lead to 272 runs. With little time left for a result, both teams agreed to a draw and shook hands.While Shakeel's effort helped Pakistan avoid defeat, his twin scores of 93 and 97 also put him on an unwanted list in Test cricket history. He became only the sixth batter to be dismissed between 90 and 99 in both innings of the same Test match.Players dismissed in the 90s twice in a Test98 & 97 C Hill bs Eng Adelaide 190295 & 93 F Woolley vs Aus Lord's 192191 & 96 G Greenidge vs Pak Georgetown 197791 & 97 G Greenidge vs NZ Christchurch 198092 & 96 M Jayawardene vs NZ Colombo SSC 200993 & 97 Saud Shakeel vs SL Rawalpindi 2026The list includes some well-known names, with Australia's Clem Hill being the first to achieve the feat in 1902. Hill scored 98 and 97 against England in Adelaide. England's Frank Woolley followed with scores of 95 and 93 against Australia at Lord's in 1921.West Indies great Gordon Greenidge features twice on the list. He scored 91 and 96 against Pakistan in Georgetown in 1977, before making 91 and 97 against New Zealand in Christchurch in 1980. Sri Lanka's Mahela Jayawardene was the last batter before Shakeel to register the unwanted distinction, scoring 92 and 96 against New Zealand in Colombo in 2009.Shakeel is the first batter since Jayawardene in 2009 to be dismissed in the nervous nineties in both innings of a Test.The draw was Pakistan's first in the current World Test Championship cycle. They have now recorded seven defeats and two wins in their previous nine matches in the cycle.The second Test will also be played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from next Tuesday. articles.title: AUS vs ENG 1st ODI: Inspired by Mitchell Johnson of 2013-14, Mahli Beardman runs through England on debut
articles.summary: CHENNAI: At a time when Australian cricket could do with some good news, 21-year-old Mahli Beardman provided a glimmer of hope.
articles.body: CHENNAI: At a time when Australian cricket could do with some good news, 21-year-old Mahli Beardman provided a glimmer of hope. The young fast bowler made an extraordinary impression on his ODI debut, claiming 6/24 in 7.4 overs to dismantle England on a lively Perth pitch in the series opener.England were bundled out for 131 in 33.4 overs, with Australia subsequently chasing down the target in 23.3 overs to seal a convincing win and take a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series. Beardman recorded the best bowling figures by an Australian on ODI debut and the fourth-best overall. He also needed just 28 deliveries to complete his five-wicket haul, the fastest by an Australian in the format.The young right-arm fast bowler has grown up admiring two fast-bowling greats — Mitchell Johnson and Dale Steyn. There was a familiar aggression to the performance, in addition to the knack of trying to pitch the ball up and inducing the edge. He got dismissed Harry Brook and Joe Root with deliveries that got the edges and followed it up with short-pitched stuff as well that completely dismantled the English line-up.It was in Oct that Beardman was going all guns blazing in Puducherry for Australia ‘A’, setting up a series win in the 50-over format. During the tour, when TOI caught up with Beardman, the pacer said: “Johnson’s 2013-14 Ashes campaign against England left a huge impression on me. Watching him bowl with that aggression really fuelled my interest in fast bowling. Steyn was my favourite. I followed him closely growing up and even tried to replicate his bowling action. Those two were my biggest inspirations,” Beardman said.Beardman values the opportunity to learn from Australia’s celebrated pace trio of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc , having already picked their brains during previous assignments. “Bowling alongside them would be a fantastic opportunity. Starc has been particularly generous with his advice, while Pat and Josh have also been helpful whenever I’ve had the chance to interact with them,” he said.Brief scores: Australia 132-3 in 23.3 overs (M Marsh 50) beat England 131 in 33.4 overs (M Beardman 6-24, S Johnson 3-42) by seven wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Starc or Lyon': David Warner makes fresh bombshell claim on ball-tampering, accuses Cricket Australia of 'cover up'
articles.summary: Former Australia opener David Warner has accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning the
articles.body: Former Australia opener David Warner has accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning the governing body's investigation into the incident.In another development in the controversy that rocked Australian cricket, Warner claimed that CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon during its investigation in the days after the Cape Town Test in 2018.Warner made the allegation in an Instagram post on Saturday, a day after accusing Test captain Pat Cummins of throwing Usman Khawaja under the bus following the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr.His latest comments came a day after Cummins addressed the allegations made in Khawaja's book during a lengthy press conference. The Australia captain dismissed the claims as “complete and utter nonsense”.“As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation,” Warner posted to Instagram.“If that’s correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?“It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. That stinks of a cover up.”The ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight after Khawaja made several claims while promoting his book, alleging that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the Cape Town Test.Cummins rejected those claims on Friday, while CA has previously said it has no intention of reopening the investigation into the incident.Warner had also responded to Cummins' comments on Friday afternoon, ahead of Australia's opening ODI of the summer against England. He said he felt "the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus".The former Australia opener followed that up with another Instagram post on Saturday, questioning the way CA handled the investigation.Warner and then captain Steve Smith were handed one-year bans by CA following the incident, while Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The inspector said police seized the budding cricketer's mobile phone and were examining its contents to establish the circumstances leading to her death. A case of suspicious death has been registered and further investigation is under way.Meanwhile, family members and relatives staged a road blockade in Vikarabad, demanding the arrest of the two youths accused of harassing her. articles.summary: MUMBAI: India women’s cricket team head coach Amol Muzumdar urged young cricketers to respect the game, embrace failure and put the team first at the
articles.body: MUMBAI: India women’s cricket team head coach Amol Muzumdar urged young cricketers to respect the game, embrace failure and put the team first at the Times Cricket Shield prize distribution function at the MCA Lounge, Wankhede Stadium, on Friday.Recalling his early days in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar spoke about the advice he received from former India batter and 1983 World Cup winner Sandeep Patil when he made his Times Shield debut for Sungrace Mafatlal in 1993. The Times Award Shield was sponsored by The Times of India Cricket Shield’s celebration partner Heineken 0.0 (Mr. Vasant Bhandari) and Sterling Reserve Packaged Drinking Water. Incidentally, this is the 96th year of the Times Shield, which started in 1930.“Score 200. What’s the big deal about scoring 100? Everyone here scores hundreds. If you have the guts, score a double hundred, then I’ll accept it,” Patil had told him. The words motivated the then 18-year-old, but his debut innings ended at 97. “As I was walking back, the captain was sitting in front of me. He gave me a smirk. That was my baptism of fire in Mumbai cricket,” Muzumdar recalled.Three months later, he scored a then world-record 260 on his firstclass debut for Mumbai against Haryana in a Ranji Trophy pre-quarterfinal in Feb 1994.Muzumdar, who went on to captain Mumbai and score 11,167 runs in 171 first-class matches, offered three lessons to youngsters.“Respect the game. That is the most important thing. The game will respect you back multifold,” he said.He also urged players not to fear failure. “Failures are part of every cricketer’s life, it’s only a question of how you respond,” he said.Highlighting the importance of the Times Shield in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar said, “The Times Shield has been an integral part of Mumbai cricket. But I can tell you one thing: It was an absolute privilege to play in the Times Cricket Shield when I first started. It’s not just a tournament, but an institution. It is probably the livelihood of so many cricketers. It gave a platform, an encouragement to so many cricketers to display their talent.“It was just an honour to play in the Times Shield when I started and even when I finished in 2013.” Former India batter and BCCI Cricket Advisory Committee member Jatin Paranjape, the other chief guest, lauded the tournament’s role in strengthening Mumbai’s club cricket.Award winners:A Division: Champions: Bank of Baroda Sports Team. articles.body: As first reported by TimesofIndia.com, fast bowler Gurnoor Brar was added to India's squad for the two-Test series against New Zealand on Saturday, while spinner Kuldeep Yadav was released to play domestic cricket.The two-Test series begins in Wellington on November 19. His best figures of 4/30 came in the second ODI against New Zealand in Wellington. In 22 first-class matches, he has picked up 71 wickets, including two five-wicket hauls.His inclusion adds another pace option to India's squad for the Test series. Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Anshul Kamboj, Akash Deep and Mohammed Siraj are the other specialist fast bowlers, while Nitish Kumar Reddy provides an additional option as an all-rounder.Kuldeep's release leaves India with two frontline spin options in Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar. articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Saturday became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history when he led Bihar in their opening match of the 2026-27 Syed
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Saturday became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history when he led Bihar in their opening match of the 2026-27 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy against Saurashtra at the Holkar Stadium in Indore.At 15 years and 232 days, Sooryavanshi broke the record previously held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who captained his national side in a T20 International at the age of 17 years and 311 days last year. Bihar won the toss and elected to bat against Saurashtra, who were led by Jaydev Unadkat.The Bihar Cricket Association (BCA) announced a 17-member squad last Friday, naming Sooryavanshi captain for the first two matches of the tournament. Suraj Kashyap was appointed vice-captain.This is not Sooryavanshi's first leadership role this year. He was named vice-captain of East Zone for the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy, serving as deputy to Ishan Kishan.With this appointment, Sooryavanshi has moved ahead of several young captains to set the record. Vukusic now stands second on the list after leading Croatia against Cyprus on August 7, 2025, at the age of 17 years and 311 days.Sooryavanshi last played during India's T20I tour of New Zealand, where he featured in two matches and scored 49 runs. Although he has been named Bihar captain for the first two matches of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he is likely to join the India A squad for the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Qatar, which begins on November 19.The 15-year-old already holds two other records in T20 cricket. Last year, he became the youngest batter to score a century in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy history, reaching the landmark in 58 balls against Maharashtra.He is also the youngest player to score a T20 century, having smashed a 35-ball hundred for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in the 2025 IPL season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Dr Simon Longstaff, the ethics expert commissioned by Cricket Australia (CA) to review the team's culture after the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal, has revealed that he heard “whispers” that more players knew about the ball-tampering plot than the three who were punished.Speaking to Nine's Weekend Today on Saturday, Longstaff said he gave senior players an opportunity to reveal anything they had not disclosed during the investigation, but nobody changed their statements.“Along the way, there were whispers, and I can't put it any more strongly than that, that something else had gone on earlier and that more people had known,” he said.“When we came to look into that – because I couldn’t turn a blind eye to it once the suggestion was made – I afforded the senior people I spoke with an opportunity … ‘Well, is there something else you want to say about the whole circumstance?’”“Nobody chose to make any alteration to their statement, so I was left with basically a blank wall. Some people saying one thing, others another, but not sufficient to be able to say there needs to be a further inquiry at that time,” he added.Longstaff questions whether CA should revisit investigationLongstaff said the whispers also suggested that ball-tampering may have taken place before the infamous Cape Town Test against South Africa.“We’re talking effectively about … good people who made bad decisions, so that’s where we looked,” he said.He could not recall whether Usman Khawaja was invited to contribute to the review, after the former Australia opener claimed in his book, Sabr, that he was never interviewed despite being willing to tell his version of events.“I can't remember exactly who it was that was given the opportunity to contribute to our review, which went much further than just the players involved,” Longstaff said.“It looked at the whole of Cricket Australia, sponsors, supporters … past Test players to see what the comparison could be. Not everybody we invited to participate in our review chose to accept that invitation. They had the liberty not to.”Longstaff also said contributions were made under strict confidentiality conditions.On Pat Cummins' denial of Khawaja's claims, Longstaff described the Australia captain's press conference as “absolutely convincing in his sincerity”.“If Cummins did not know, and I believe he didn't, then not everybody knew. articles.title: Sandpaper scandal: David Warner accuses Cricket Australia of 'cover-up'
articles.summary: Former vice-captain David Warner accuses Cricket Australia of a "cover-up", claiming Australia's bowlers were not interviewed in ball-tampering investigation.
articles.body:
David Warner has accused Cricket Australia (CA) of a "cover up" as the row over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal continued.

Former vice-captain Warner, captain Steve Smith and opener Cameron Bancroft all served lengthy bans as part of CA's investigation into the ball-tampering scandal that rocked Australian cricket during a Test series in South Africa in 2018.

Batter Usman Khawaja has reopened discussions about the scandal with explosive claims in his new autobiography, where he said the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

And Warner has questioned the investigation into the incident by claiming that Australia's bowlers from the Cape Town Test were not interviewed.

"As far as l am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner said.

"If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know?

"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.

The four frontline bowlers - Hazlewood, Starc, Lyon and Pat Cummins - have maintained they did not know about the plan to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

Cummins, Australia's Test captain since 2021, said in his extraordinary news conference on Friday that he was interviewed as part of the investigation.

In response to Warner's comments, CA said: "As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since.

"Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events."

Watch on iPlayer: The Sandpapergate Scandal

'Gloves are off' - how Australian papers reacted to Cummins on Khawaja

Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'

Warner has been steadfast in his defence of former batting partner and childhood friend Khawaja since his recollections were made public last week.

After Cummins' news conference, in which he said suggestions the entire team knew about the scheme to cheat were "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense", Warner said: "I stick with Uzzie. It's the truth. The captain threw Uzzie under the bus.

"I feel it was a botched investigation."

Khawaja also revealed he was not interviewed as part of the investigation, despite sitting next to Bancroft - the player seen with sandpaper on the field - in the dressing room.

CA has said it will not reopen its investigation.

articles.summary: David Warner has issued fresh claims that three of Australia's bowlers, who played during the infamous 2018 Test match against South Africa in Cape Town, were not interviewed by Cricket Australia as part of their investigations into the ball-tampering scandal
articles.body:
Usman Khawaja's claims in his new autobiography reignited the controversy that rocked Australian cricket eight years ago, with the former opening batter stating that the entire Australian team knew sandpaper was being used to alter the ball before their Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.

Warner has now doubled down on his criticisms of Cricket Australia's probe into the saga , claiming they had not interviewed three of the bowlers - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon - who featured in that Test, as part of what he called a "shoddy investigation".

"As far as I am aware, CA [Cricket Australia] did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner wrote in a post on Instagram.

"If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that their bowlers didn't know?

"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.

A Cricket Australia spokesperson told Sky Sports News : "As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since

"Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events."

Cricket Australia will not open new investigation

Previously, Warner had said Cricket Australia's investigation into the sandpaper scandal was "rushed and botched" , with the former opener issuing his support to Khawaja during a statement issued on Monday.

In his autobiography ' Sabr: Finding my way in cricket and in life' , Khawaja said he was not called for an interview by Cricket Australia in the wake of sandpapergate.

Warner and then-captain Steve Smith both received 12-month bans, while Cameron Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension.

Cummins, Starc, Lyon and Hazlewood were not punished and issued a joint statement in 2021 explaining they had no knowledge that ball-tampering was taking place.

On Saturday, Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg told Australian radio station SEN that the governing body would not be re-opening the investigation.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," Greenberg said.

"I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman [Khawaja], and our position hasn't changed on that.

"There's absolutely no benefit in going back, that's the clear position of the CA board. I think it's fine, we've got to look ahead, and the matter was dealt with under a previous leadership back in 2018.

"Trying to second-guess decisions from a previous time or making an assessment through the prism of hindsight is not something we want to do."

He added: "When you cut to the core of the challenge that we face here, Usman's version of events is inconsistent with what others have had to say.

"I can assure you there are lots of other players who have a very, very different version of events. And they have made that very public from the very start of 2018, they have been very consistent in their position right through until today.

"From my conversations with many over the weekend, I don't think that will change either."

Following Khawaja's revelations, both Cummins and Starc have denied any knowledge of sandpapergate, with the current Australia captain rejecting Khawaja's claims during a press conference on Friday.

"When he [Khawaja] says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, ​he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," ‌Cummins told reporters.

Warner, though, hit back at the Australian Test captain's comments, saying he had "thrown Khawaja under a bus".

"Pat Cummins was very well-prepared this morning [Friday]. I still stick by Uzzie, and what he's written in that book," Warner said.

"It is the truth, and I really, really support him. I actually feel for him at the moment; I feel that the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus, and I'm very, very disappointed about that.

"All three of us have paid a big price in this. I hadn't spoken to 'Banger' [Bancroft] in eight years, but at the end of the day, we have to live with these consequences daily. We've got to live with these consequences daily, and we've been served a life punishment.

"So, when other people talk about how they've been affected by it, there's nothing worse for me, Steve [Smith] and Cameron [Bancroft], who have to walk out there every single day.

"We cop abuse. Yes, we accepted it. But my wife and I paid the greatest price; we lost a baby during that time. That's why it really hurts me the most, until the truth is accepted."
