articles.body: Former India spinner Murali Kartik has backed Usman Khawaja in the ongoing debate over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning Pat Cummins' claim that he was unaware of the plan to use sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.The controversy resurfaced after Khawaja made several claims in his memoir, Sabr, suggesting that the entire Australian team, including current Test captain Cummins, knew about the plan to alter the condition of the ball.Cummins rejected the allegations during a press conference on Friday, describing Khawaja's claims as "complete and utter nonsense".Kartik, however, sided with Khawaja and said it was difficult to believe that the bowlers were unaware of a plan that was allegedly being carried out for their benefit."When it happened, there was a mini probe and three players were sent to the galley. Everyone knew what was happening. The problem is that if and when something like this happens, it's for the sake of the bowlers. 'Devious, underhand, wrong' - let's not go there. Once that is happening, and if I am the bowler while the other two guys are doing it for me, I don't know how anyone can say that I didn't know about it. How can anyone say that?" Kartik said on Cricbuzz.He also questioned why only three players were held responsible for the incident, arguing that the bowlers would have been informed if the plan was intended to help them."I was surprised that only three guys had to bear the brunt of it. Everybody, all the bowlers, would've known. When you're trying to do something for the sake of the bowlers, wouldn't you tell the bowlers? How can anyone believe that? Are we in kindergarten to accept that sort of thing? There have been so many murmurs: 'Oh, Warner is going to come out with a tell-all. Warner is going to tell the story once he is done with everything.' It's not him, it's Usman Khawaja who has come out and said that everybody knew. I am pretty sure everybody knew," he added.Warner accuses Cricket Australia of cover-upThe debate has also drawn a fresh response from former Australia opener David Warner, who accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.Warner, who received a one-year ban for his role in the incident, questioned the governing body's investigation, claiming that it did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Starc or Nathan Lyon."As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," he said on Instagram."If that's correct then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know?"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea."That stinks of a cover-up."The controversy returned to the spotlight this week after Khawaja released his autobiography, in which he alleged that the entire team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to rough up the ball and make it swing.Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft knew about the plan. All three were sent home from South Africa following the incident.Cummins addressed Khawaja's claims during a lengthy press conference on Friday, describing them as "100 percent wrong". Warner subsequently accused the Australia captain of throwing his close friend Khawaja "under the bus".Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Bhool gaya’ moment! Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s hilarious response at toss on record-breaking captaincy debut - Watch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had a memorable and amusing moment during his historic captaincy debut on Saturday when the 15-year-old forgot Bihar's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had a memorable and amusing moment during his historic captaincy debut on Saturday when the 15-year-old forgot Bihar's playing XI after winning the toss against Saurashtra in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 opener at the Holkar Stadium.Asked about his team's combination after opting to bat, Sooryavanshi responded with a smile: "I think, sir, bhool gaya lagta main (I think, sir, I have forgotten)."The light-hearted exchange quickly became a talking point on a landmark day for the teenage batting sensation, who became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history at 15 years and 232 days.Sooryavanshi broke the previous record held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who had captained his national side at 17 years and 311 days in a T20 International against Cyprus on August 7, 2025.'Dream come true': Sooryavanshi on leading BiharThe Bihar youngster described the opportunity to captain his home state as a special moment, expressing gratitude for being entrusted with the responsibility.“It feels like a dream come true because I started playing cricket here, and getting the opportunity to lead the same state is a big thing. I am very grateful, and I will try to fulfil the responsibility given to me to the best of my ability," he said.WATCH:Bihar handed Sooryavanshi the leadership role for their first two matches of the domestic T20 competition. The appointment marks another milestone in his rapid rise, having made his India debut just five months ago. He was also named vice-captain of East Zone for the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy, deputising for Ishan Kishan.His first outing as Bihar captain, however, did not produce a substantial contribution with the bat. Sooryavanshi scored 18 off 12 deliveries before being caught and bowled by left-arm pacer Chetan Sakariya.Bihar managed 137/9 in their 20 overs, with Prithvi Raj top-scoring with 38. Saurashtra chased down the target in 16.3 overs to register a five-wicket victory. Harvansh Pangalia led the chase with 33 off just 11 balls, hitting three sixes and three fours.Short SMAT stint before India A assignmentSooryavanshi is expected to feature in only one more SMAT match before joining India A for the ACC Rising Stars Emerging tournament in Doha from November 19.His latest international outing came during India's T20I tour of New Zealand, where he scored 49 runs in two matches. His 19-ball 45, featuring in a 133-run opening stand with Abhishek Sharma in just 7.1 overs, was among the highlights of India's 3-2 series victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘I’ll know straight away’: Wasim Akram questions Pat Cummins’ Sandpapergate defence
articles.summary: Pakistan legend Wasim Akram has questioned Pat Cummins' claim that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering incident during the infamous 2018 Cape Town
articles.body: Pakistan legend Wasim Akram has questioned Pat Cummins' claim that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering incident during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test, arguing that an experienced bowler would immediately recognise if sandpaper had been used on the ball.The Sandpapergate controversy has returned to the spotlight following Usman Khawaja's explosive claims in his book, Sabr, that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper. With David Warner backing Khawaja and Cummins strongly rejecting the allegations, the row shows little sign of dying down.Akram, one of the finest exponents of reverse swing, weighed in on the debate, explaining why the scratches caused by sandpaper would be noticeably different from the marks produced through conventional ball maintenance.Akram questions Cummins' claim: 'I'll know straight away'Akram said he was surprised by Cummins' statement, given his role as a bowler during the Cape Town Test."I saw Pat Cummins, who's a very close friend of mine, a great cricketer and one of the top leaders in world cricket, saying that he didn't know. So probably the team didn't know at the time what was happening, in my opinion. It's my opinion. It can be right or wrong."But as a bowler, when the cricket ball comes in my hand, either it's the fifth over, either it's in the 10th over, or either it's in the 50th over, the old ball, where you look after the ball, you shine the one side; if it's a dry day, dry square, you one bounce throw, you get scratch a bit. But the sandpaper scratch is totally different from the one-bounce scratch," Akram said in a video posted on social media.The former Pakistan captain challenged cricket fans to examine the difference themselves by rubbing sandpaper on a semi-new ball."And as a cricket lover, if you want to check, grab a semi-new cricket ball, grab a piece of sandpaper, and rub it in; you know, the scratches are totally different," he said.Akram clarified that he was not taking sides in the dispute but stressed that honesty was central to Australia's cricketing reputation."So again, as I said, I'm not taking anybody's sides. And Australians are known and famous for their straightforwardness, hardness on the field, off the field, and most importantly, honesty. And I think that's what the whole nation has been, you know, under stress a bit, obviously, eight years ago and back to it again. I hope things get sorted out," he added.He reiterated his belief that an experienced bowler would recognise unusual damage to the ball."This is my take on this issue: as a bowler, especially an experienced bowler, I'll have a look at the ball, and I'll know straight away something is not right," he concluded.Cummins calls Khawaja's allegations 'complete and utter nonsense'Cummins has firmly rejected Khawaja's suggestion that the entire Australian side knew about the sandpaper plan."When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong," Cummins said."I've said that consistently for the last eight years, I did not know that was happening. But I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam (Bancroft) to be careful when using sandpaper," he added.With Warner continuing to support Khawaja, former Australia captain Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft also part of the original sanctions, and questions now being raised by Akram, the controversy sparked by Khawaja's revelations looks far from over.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: India teenager becomes youngest captain in men's T20 cricket
articles.summary: Teenage India sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks the record held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic as the youngest captain in top-level men's Twenty20 cricket.
articles.body:
Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has become the youngest captain in top-level men's Twenty20 cricket after taking charge of his state side Bihar on Saturday.

Captaining at the age of 15 years and 232 days, Sooryavanshi broke the record held by Zach Vukusic, who captained Croatia aged 17 years and 311 days.

Bihar lost their opening match in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy - India's domestic state T20 competition, below the Indian Premier League (IPL) - by five wickets to Saurashtra, with Sooryavanshi making 18 from 12 balls.

It is the latest landmark the young career of Sooryavanshi, who became India's youngest men's international in July when he made his T20 debut against England.

He has broken numerous records since making his IPL debut for Rajasthan Royals as a 14-year-old in 2025, becoming the franchise tournament's youngest player.

He became the youngest centurion in men's T20s when hitting a hundred against Gujarat Titans later that season, and this year was the tournament's leading run-scorer.

Sooryavanshi played in two of India's five T20 internationals in New Zealand earlier this month, with a top score of 45 in the third match in Wellington.

He is also due to be part of India's side at the Rising Stars Asia Cup, a development 50-over tournament which takes place in Doha later this month.

articles.title: 'You can't completely surrender': Ex-India cricketer's blunt assessment after Matt Henry's six-wicket demolition
articles.summary: India's batting collapse in the fourth ODI against New Zealand has prompted serious questions about the team's approach, with head coach Gautam Gambhir
articles.body: India's batting collapse in the fourth ODI against New Zealand has prompted serious questions about the team's approach, with head coach Gautam Gambhir expressing concern over repeated failures and former India opener Aakash Chopra backing his call for greater responsibility from the batters.India endured a disastrous start to their 334-run chase at Mount Maunganui on Friday, losing Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer without scoring by the end of the opening over. Another wicket fell before the end of the sixth over, and the visitors eventually crumbled to 89, suffering a humiliating 244-run defeat. It was India's second-heaviest loss in ODI cricket.Chopra, analysing the defeat on ESPNcricinfo, echoed Gambhir's assessment that the Indian batters needed to show greater application rather than surrender against quality bowling."As Gautam Gambhir mentioned after the match, there are no unplayable deliveries in the game of cricket. Yes, it was great bowling, but you need to be better. And that's the way to look at it. You can't completely surrender. You have to find a way. It's just that it happened so quickly that you really didn't have the time to recover, regroup, reassess and play differently," Aakash Chopra said.Much of India's misery was orchestrated by Matt Henry, who dismantled the top order before completing a six-wicket haul. The New Zealand fast bowler returned figures of 9.4-2-27-6, leaving the Indian batters struggling to cope with his movement and accuracy.Chopra pointed out that Henry's effectiveness increases considerably in the longer white-ball format, particularly when conditions offer assistance to the new ball."He didn't look as menacing in the T20Is. But the moment the format gets longer, there are two new balls, and there's a bit in the surface, that's when Matt Henry becomes a very difficult bowler to negotiate early on when the ball is new. When you see the ball coming out of his hand, there's hardly any indication of which way it's going to go after pitching," Chopra said.Gambhir, meanwhile, made it clear that India's batting troubles could not be dismissed as an isolated failure. The head coach also referred to the team's vulnerability during the rain-affected second ODI, when India slipped to 111/7 while pursuing a modest target of 135 before eventually securing victory through the DLS method.The repeated collapses have become a concern for the Indian camp, even though the visitors continue to lead the five-match series 2-1. With the final ODI scheduled at Mount Maunganui on Sunday, Gambhir will be hoping for a more convincing display from his batters."There's no benefit to sweeping it under the carpet. It isn't just this match. Even in the previous match, we were seven down for 111 or 112. Today we lost, so we are talking about it," Gambhir said in his post-match press conference on Friday."Yeah, it's a huge defeat, no doubt about it, but even in the previous match, if you're chasing 135, and you get seven down for 111, obviously it is a bit of a concern, because yes, there is some help here for the bowlers, so we have to be not only mentally but from the skill point of view we need to be ready as well," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'The side will pose a unique set of challenges': Will Young wary of Jasprit Bumrah threat ahead of India Test series
articles.summary: New Zealand batter Will Young believes India's bowling attack will become even more challenging with the return of Jasprit Bumrah for the upcoming
articles.body: New Zealand batter Will Young believes India's bowling attack will become even more challenging with the return of Jasprit Bumrah for the upcoming two-match Test series, but has backed the Black Caps' own bowling unit to give the visitors an equally difficult examination. With both teams eyeing a place in next year's World Test Championship (WTC) final, the series promises to be a significant contest in the race for the summit clash.The two-match series, beginning November 19, will be India's first red-ball assignment against New Zealand since suffering a shocking 3-0 whitewash at home in 2024. Bumrah, who missed India's series-winning tour of Sri Lanka in August due to a knee injury, is set to return for the crucial contest, adding considerable strength to the Indian pace attack.Young acknowledged the threat posed by the Indian pace spearhead but insisted that New Zealand's bowlers have the ability to challenge India's batting line-up on home soil.Will Young highlights Bumrah threat, backs New Zealand bowlersSpeaking to reporters on the eve of the ODI series decider on Saturday, Young said the previous Test series between the two sides was now in the past and that both teams would face a fresh set of challenges in the upcoming contest."I think that the Test series that we had in India a couple of years ago is long gone. We've got a brand-new challenge in front of us which is two massive Tests against India at home. It's at Wellington and Christchurch, two of the marquee Test venues in New Zealand I'd like to think. So it's going to be a completely different set of challenges," Young said.The New Zealand batter described Bumrah as one of the best bowlers in world cricket and acknowledged that his presence would test the hosts. However, he was equally confident about his team's bowling resources and expected India's batters to face a stern examination."As you said, Bumrah coming into the side will pose a unique set of challenges with that as well. He's one of the best bowlers in the world. So we've got our work cut out for us, but I think we've got some brilliant bowlers too. So the Indian batsmen will have to adapt to what we bring to the Test series too. So as I said before, it's all set for a really interesting two-Test match series," he added.India and New Zealand eye crucial WTC pointsThe upcoming series carries significant importance in the World Test Championship standings, with both teams firmly in contention for a place in the 2027 final at The Oval.New Zealand, the inaugural WTC champions in 2021, are currently second in the standings behind table-toppers and defending champions South Africa. India, meanwhile, occupy fourth place as they look to return to the summit clash after finishing runners-up in the first two editions.timGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who will replace Rishabh Pant? Ex-India opener reveals LSG's two leading captaincy options
articles.summary: Lucknow Super Giants' decision to bring Kuldeep Yadav on board through a trade could prove to be one of their most influential moves ahead of IPL 2027,
articles.body: Lucknow Super Giants' decision to bring Kuldeep Yadav on board through a trade could prove to be one of their most influential moves ahead of IPL 2027, according to former India opener Abhinav Mukund. He believes the left-arm wrist-spinner has the ability to transform LSG's bowling attack and potentially play a decisive role in their pursuit of a maiden IPL title.Kuldeep joined LSG shortly after the conclusion of IPL 2026, with the franchise completing a trade deal with Delhi Capitals that saw wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant move in the opposite direction.Mukund believes Kuldeep's wicket-taking ability makes him an invaluable addition, particularly at the Ekana Stadium, where conditions are expected to assist spin bowling. He also highlighted the prospect of Kuldeep forming an attacking partnership with fellow spinner Digvesh Rathi.“Kuldeep Yadav is a phenomenal signing for Lucknow Super Giants. He is a genuine wicket-taking spinner, and in T20 cricket, that is worth its weight in gold.“He does not just keep the runs down, he looks for wickets in the middle overs, and that changes the game for a captain. At the Ekana Stadium, where the pitch offers help to spinners, he will be even more dangerous. His partnership with Digvesh Rathi could be one of the most exciting spin pairings in the IPL.“Both of them are attacking bowlers who are not afraid to toss the ball up and invite the batters to go after them, because they know their variations can get them out. When you have two spinners asking different questions, it becomes very hard for the opposition to settle. If they build a strong understanding, LSG will have a spin attack that can win them games on its own and for me, this trade could be one of the smartest moves of the season,” Mukund told JioStar.However, while Kuldeep's arrival strengthens the bowling department, LSG still have an important decision to make regarding their leadership. Pant's exit has left the franchise searching for a new captain as they prepare for another attempt at winning their first IPL trophy.Mukund identified Aiden Markram and Nicholas Pooran as the two leading candidates currently available within the squad. Both have experience captaining franchise teams in different T20 leagues. However, he believes LSG could also explore the possibility of bringing in an experienced Indian player through the trade window.“Lucknow Super Giants are on the hunt for a captain. Now it depends on their team management about what they prefer, whether they prefer to appoint a captain from a player in their squad or whether they choose someone from the mini auction. The strongest option within the squad is Aiden Markram.“He leads their SA20 side, Durban’s Super Giants, which makes his case for leading LSG quite strong. Then Nicholas Pooran is an option too, because he captains MI New York and the Trinbago Knight Riders as well, so he’s a good option too. So they have good options in their squad, but the trade window could change things.“If LSG find a senior Indian player who can lead the side, they might look at that option instead. An Indian captain is always easier to manage in the IPL because they understand the local players and the pressure that comes with the role. So, while Markram and Pooran are strong candidates, LSG should keep their options open going into the auction,” he added.With Kuldeep strengthening their spin resources and the captaincy question still unresolved, LSG have a crucial period ahead as they look to assemble a combination capable of challenging for the IPL 2027 title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs England: Harry Brook hoping for improved performance despite lack of training session ahead of second ODI
articles.summary: England will not be able to train in the nets ahead of their second ODI against Australia in Adelaide; the team is set to fly to South Australia for the match, which commences at 3.30am, UK time, on Sunday
articles.body:
Brook's side were skittled for 131 before succumbing to a thumping seven-wicket defeat in their ODI opener at Perth's Optus Stadium on Friday.

Undone by the unique sharp bounce of Western Australia they now face a different proposition as they head south, but with a two-and-a-half hour evening flight to factor in, they will not get a chance to work on things ahead of a must-win second match.

With England keen to ready themselves for next year's World Cup campaign in South Africa, Brook is not shying away from a tight schedule.

"Cricket, and especially white-ball cricket, comes so thick and fast and you've got to be able to and be prepared to move on very quickly," Brook said.

"We've got to adapt to conditions as quickly as possible. We're not going to have a training session, we've got a flight and then we're pretty much straight into the game.

"But that replicates what the World Cup's going to show us and there's going to be some great lessons for us going from this sort of surface in Perth to Adelaide, where it's going to be slightly lower and probably not as quick.

"It's a good opportunity for us to learn some lessons and work towards that World Cup. I won't dwell [on the loss] too much. You've got to learn and you learn a lot from defeats, probably more than you do from your victories."

England's bowling attack barely stood a chance of defending such a slender total on Friday, meaning the decision to once again omit Adil Rashid slipped under the radar.

The leg-spinner is the second-highest wicket-taker for England in 50-over cricket behind James Anderson and has been a guaranteed pick for a dozen years. Now, at the age of 38, he finds himself battling for his spot.

He made a single appearance in the recent tri-series in Pakistan, with left-armer Liam Dawson preferred in what was explained as a horses-for-courses selection, and was overlooked again in Perth.

Brook, who called the Yorkshireman a "magician" on the eve of the game, credited that call to the pace of the pitch but will soon find himself running out of reasons if Rashid continues to miss out on a more helpful Adelaide track.

"We knew that the surface was going to be seam-friendly and spin wasn't going to play a massive part, hence why we went with Daws [Liam Dawson], who is probably a better batter than Rash at the minute," he said.

articles.title: 'He actually got emotional': R Ashwin reveals Virat Kohli's reaction to his retirement decision
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has opened up about an emotional conversation with Virat Kohli at the Gabba during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, recalling how
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has opened up about an emotional conversation with Virat Kohli at the Gabba during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, recalling how the former India captain was left emotional after learning about his decision to retire from international cricket.The former India off-spinner revealed that the conversation took place on the balcony in Brisbane during a rain interruption. What began as an informal discussion between the two eventually turned into a heartfelt exchange, with Kohli speaking about the future of India's Test team and the challenges surrounding its transition.Speaking on a podcast with Aakash Chopra, Ashwin explained that retirement had been on his mind for several months before he finally called time on his career in December 2024.He disclosed that he had first contemplated the decision as early as March 2024, despite enjoying an excellent run with the ball. However, persistent knee problems were affecting his batting. Head coach Gautam Gambhir subsequently urged him to continue until the end of India's 2024 home season.The home Test series against New Zealand, in which India suffered a whitewash, proved particularly disappointing for Ashwin. He felt he was no longer able to deliver match-winning performances for the team.His decision became firmer after he was left out of India's playing XI for the opening Test against Australia in Perth. When an opportunity arose during the Brisbane Test, Ashwin found himself alone with Kohli during a rain break and decided to share his thoughts.“In that game, I didn’t go there to tell Virat and it was raining; I sat with him only because he was sitting alone," Ashwin remembered.Ashwin also reflected on how his relationship with Kohli had evolved over the years. The two had experienced differences in the past, but the former spinner said their equation improved following the COVID break. During their conversation at the Gabba, Kohli began discussing his own batting, the state of the Indian Test side and the challenges ahead during a period of transition.“My relationship with Virat improved after the COVID break. I realized that if there were any disappointments in my mind, it wasn’t his fault. I tried to speak to him about that; I was forthcoming. I had nothing selfish to to say. But he started speaking his mind: what he was thinking about his batting, how he looked at the Indian Test team, what it needed in a transition. He was talking like a leader, how there were these basic problems in the team and so on. I listened."The conversation took an unexpected turn when Kohli sought Ashwin's opinion on the team's future. Ashwin encouraged him to continue leading the side, pointing towards his fitness and ability to make a difference. However, he then revealed that he had already made up his mind to walk away from international cricket.“I said ‘You can definitely do it, you’re fit. Maybe it’s a question of discipline, tactics, but you can.’ I told him that my opinion doesn’t matter, because I’m leaving. He said, ‘What are you saying?’ I said I’m retiring today. He actually got emotional. He asked how I decided and if it was instinctive; I said it just happened. I told him I enjoyed playing alongside him."Ashwin further recalled telling Kohli how much he valued his contributions to Indian cricket, both as captain and as a fielder. Despite representing the same team, the two had often been competitive about their respective contributions, but the spinner wanted to acknowledge the respect he had for his former teammate.“I told him that, ‘I haven’t told you this much, but I valued your contribution as captain and as a fielder. I’m extremely blessed to have shared the dressing room with you people. You are one of the greats.’ Then we hugged."Ashwin announced his retirement after the Brisbane Test, bringing an end to a distinguished international career. articles.title: 'I was envious': R Ashwin makes honest confession about Ravindra Jadeja
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has offered an interesting account of what made his bowling partnership with Ravindra Jadeja so successful, revealing how he learned
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has offered an interesting account of what made his bowling partnership with Ravindra Jadeja so successful, revealing how he learned to use the left-arm spinner's strengths and limitations to his advantage. Ashwin described Jadeja as an exceptionally gifted cricketer but suggested that the all-rounder initially lacked the instinct to consistently find ways to dismiss batters.The two formed one of the most successful spin combinations in Test cricket, sharing the field in 58 matches and accounting for 587 wickets. While Ashwin claimed 317 of those dismissals, Jadeja contributed 270. According to the former India off-spinner, their success stemmed from understanding each other's contrasting approaches and making the most of them.Speaking on Aakash Chopra's podcast show, Baith & Bol, Ashwin explained that he understood Jadeja's game well enough to help him operate within his strengths rather than push him towards something that did not come naturally to him.“I know his limitations well," Ashwin said. “Very few can bring him out of those limitations. I was one of them. His biggest strength: naturally gifted. If he has a bad day, you just tell him your effort is fine; tomorrow will be better. His action was simple, release point simple, tappa so good—he doesn’t have to think. He didn’t know how to dismiss batsmen—I’m saying he absolutely didn’t know. But his skill to choke batsmen was intertwined with his skill. You can’t sweep him—trajectory is low. You can’t step out—airspeed is good. You can’t play defense without doubting if the ball would remain the same."One aspect of Jadeja's bowling that often came under scrutiny was his reluctance to vary his pace or give the ball more flight, even when the conditions called for it. Ashwin revealed that he had attempted to persuade his spin partner to experiment more, but those efforts often came at the expense of Jadeja's effectiveness and economy.Eventually, Ashwin recognised that Jadeja's ability to keep things tight from one end gave him the freedom to attack from the other. While Jadeja restricted the opposition's scoring opportunities, Ashwin could experiment with different deliveries and concentrate on taking wickets. That combination also made Jadeja more difficult to deal with.Ashwin said developing this understanding gave him even greater appreciation for what Jadeja brought to the team, particularly his remarkable consistency and control.“When I understood that, my respect for Jadeja doubled—what he does is not easy. I have seen many skillful spinners, but the repetitive nature- keeping the ball there at the same speed is very difficult. Spinning the ball at that speed is not easy," he said.Ashwin also spoke candidly about experiencing a sense of envy towards Jadeja's natural abilities, although he clarified that he was never jealous of his teammate's success. What stood out to him was the ease with which Jadeja could excel across different aspects of the game without having to put in the same kind of conscious experimentation.Responding to Chopra's question about what made him envious, Ashwin listed Jadeja's remarkable all-round abilities, from bowling and fielding to batting, and admitted that he often wondered what he could have achieved with similar natural gifts.“A person who doesn’t experiment in the nets, but if you give him the ball, he’ll land on tappa, good speed, rotation, takes catches in the field, runs like a bullet, moves like silk, connects every second direct hit, has every batting shot, power, skill, defense against spinners, developed against fast bowlers, scored 300 in Ranji Trophy. It was all natural! However much we’d work hard to get close to him, his skill was still bigger. I often thought if I had that skill, I’d rule the world. But it is what it is. He was so skillful that he didn’t have to think much."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohit Ulva stars as India U19 chase down 338 in last-ball thriller to beat Pakistan by one wicket and clinch Asia Cup title
articles.summary: In a final that had everything, India U19 pulled off a sensational one-wicket victory over Pakistan to clinch the Under-19 Asia Cup title in a last-ball
articles.body: In a final that had everything, India U19 pulled off a sensational one-wicket victory over Pakistan to clinch the Under-19 Asia Cup title in a last-ball thriller on Saturday. Just when the defending champions looked certain to seal the trophy, number 10 batter Mohit Ulva produced a breathtaking unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls to guide India home in a remarkable 339-run chase.India, who were chasing a daunting target of 338, finished at 339/9 in 49.6 overs, with Ulva smashing the winning boundary off the final delivery. Chigurupati Venkata remained unbeaten on 11 as the Indian players stormed onto the field to celebrate an unforgettable triumph.Usman Khan's century powers Pakistan to 337/9Earlier, opener Usman Khan led Pakistan's batting effort with a brilliant 107 off 106 balls, helping the defending champions post 337/9 in their allotted 50 overs. Usman shared a 62-run opening stand with Hayam Khan before combining with Abdul Qadir for a massive 135-run partnership. Qadir played an aggressive knock of 80 off just 54 deliveries, bringing up his maiden Youth ODI half-century in 39 balls.Captain Farhan Yousaf added further impetus with a 60-run contribution off 63 deliveries, taking Pakistan past the 300-run mark. For India, Kavya Patel was the standout bowler with four wickets for 68 runs, while C Venkata claimed three wickets for 40 runs.Sehwag, Raichandani give India a solid startIndia began the chase positively, with openers Aaryavir Sehwag and captain Lakshya Raichandani putting together a 90-run opening partnership. Sehwag continued his impressive tournament with a fluent 58 off 61 deliveries, including nine boundaries. Despite taking a blow on his forearm during the powerplay, the opener battled through the discomfort and brought up another half-century.Raichandani provided stability at the other end, registering his third half-century of the tournament. The Indian skipper eventually departed for a well-made 80 off 101 balls, with Anvay Dravid following him back to the pavilion after being run out for 19.VK Vineeth contributed 24 before falling to Rizwanullah, who also dismissed Arjun Rajput for 16. Pakistan continued to chip away at the Indian batting order, leaving the chase in serious trouble.Mohit Ulva produces a stunning rescue actIndia's hopes took another major hit when Yashbardhan Chauhan and Kavya Patel departed in quick succession. With wickets falling at regular intervals, Pakistan appeared firmly in control of the contest. However, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva had other plans. The duo launched a remarkable counterattack, putting together a 57-run partnership that brought India back into the contest.Manal smashed 47 off just 32 deliveries, hitting three fours and three sixes, while Ulva kept attacking from the other end. Manal's dismissal in the 48th over left India needing 29 runs off 17 balls with just one wicket remaining.Ulva refused to give up, taking the attack to Pakistan's bowlers. He smashed Mohammad Sayyam for two boundaries and a six in the 49th over, reducing the equation to eight runs from the final six deliveries.Last-ball drama as India snatch victoryWith Pakistan needing just one wicket to seal the title, Ahmed Hussain was handed the responsibility of bowling the final over.Ulva and Venkata kept their composure under immense pressure, collecting crucial singles to bring the equation down to three runs off the final delivery. With the match hanging in the balance, Ulva stepped down the track and smashed Hussain's delivery towards wide long-off. The ball bounced once before racing to the boundary, sparking wild celebrations in the Indian camp.Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, agonisingly missing out on a half-century but delivering one of the most memorable knocks in an India-Pakistan age-group final.India finished at 339/9 to complete a remarkable one-wicket victory and lift the Under-19 Asia Cup trophy in dramatic fashion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is Mohit Ulva? The India U-19 star who hit the last-ball boundary to seal Asia Cup triumph over Pakistan
articles.summary: Mohit Ulva kept his cool when it mattered most.
articles.body: Mohit Ulva kept his cool when it mattered most. With India needing three runs off the final ball against Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, the 18-year-old right-hand batter smashed leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain wide of long-off for a boundary to script a stunning one-wicket victory and bring the trophy back to India.Chasing a daunting 338, India were staring at defeat at 252 for eight in the 42nd over. But Ulva and Manal Chauhan turned the contest around with a courageous 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. While Manal contributed 47 off 32 balls, Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, taking responsibility for the tense final stages of the chase.After Manal's dismissal at 302, India still needed 36 runs with just one wicket in hand. Ulva then found an equally determined partner in No. 11 C Venkata, who made an unbeaten 11 off eight balls. The duo brought the equation down to eight runs off the final over before Ulva delivered the decisive blow on the last ball.But who is the teenager who emerged as India's unlikely hero on the biggest stage?From tennis-ball cricket in his village to India's U-19 teamAn 18-year-old right-arm medium pacer and right-hand batter, Ulva's cricketing journey began with tennis-ball cricket in his village. His father, who works with the Railway Protection Force, recognised his potential and encouraged him to pursue the sport through formal academy training.Ulva subsequently joined the Cricket Bungalow in Jamnagar, where he trained under Mahendrasinh Chauhan, the coach who also guided India all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja.From off-spin to fast bowlingInterestingly, Ulva did not begin his cricketing journey as a fast bowler. He initially trained as an off-spinner. However, Chauhan spotted an opportunity to develop another aspect of his game.Considering Ulva's lean physique and ability to run well, the coach suggested that he try fast bowling. That advice eventually helped shape him into a right-arm medium pacer.Ulva progressed through Saurashtra's age-group cricket system before earning his place in the India Under-19 squad.A match-winning moment against PakistanThe Asia Cup final could well prove to be a defining moment in Ulva's young career. Ulva's match-winning effort came after India were pushed to the brink of defeat in their chase of Pakistan's 338-run target. The opening pair of Aaryavir Sehwag (58) and captain Lakshya Raichandani (80) added 95 runs, but a middle-order collapse left India struggling at 252 for eight in the 42nd over.With Pakistan closing in on victory, Ulva joined Manal Chauhan at the crease and the duo produced a remarkable fightback. Their 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket kept India's hopes alive, with Manal scoring 47 off 32 balls and Ulva contributing 49 not out off just 26 deliveries.Manal did much of the running between the wickets during their crucial stand before departing at 302, leaving India needing 36 runs with just one wicket remaining. Ulva then found support from No. 11 C Venkata (11 not out off eight balls), and the pair brought the equation down to eight runs off the final over.With three runs needed off the last delivery, Ulva smashed Pakistan leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain wide of long-off for a boundary to seal India's stunning one-wicket victory and U-19 Asia Cup title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins and his wife Rebecca have finally sold their investment property in Moss Vale, in the Southern Highlands of New
articles.body: Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins and his wife Rebecca have finally sold their investment property in Moss Vale, in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales, after an eight-month search for a buyer. The 1920s Californian bungalow is understood to have fetched around $1.16 million, although the official sale price has not been disclosed.The property was listed in March with a price guide of $1.25 million to $1.295 million. Richardson & Wrench agents Georgia Soster and Frank Walsh handled the sale. The time taken to secure a buyer was considerably longer than the local market average, with realestate.com.au calculating a median of 72 days on the market for more than 100 four-bedroom homes sold in the area over the past year.Inside Pat Cummins and Rebecca’s Southern Highlands propertySet behind established hedges on a sprawling 2,327-square-metre block, the three-bedroom bungalow features coffered ceilings, timber floors, brick fireplaces and an enclosed veranda overlooking the garden. The property also includes a vegetable patch, a chicken yard and a double garage, with turpentine and cypress pine among the timber details.Cummins and Rebecca, an interior designer, purchased the property in 2017 for $905,000. It was subsequently used as a rental, reportedly generating around $550 a week. The property's marketing campaign also highlighted its medium-density development potential, subject to council approval.Moss Vale property market and the couple’s Bronte plansThe sale comes against the backdrop of a relatively subdued market in Moss Vale. The median sale price for four-bedroom houses currently stands at $1,532,500, reflecting an annual increase of 0.5 per cent. The figure remains below the suburb’s previous peaks of $1.8 million, recorded in both 2022 and 2024.Meanwhile, Cummins and Rebecca are reportedly planning renovations to their $16 million home in Bronte. In January, the couple also purchased the adjoining semi-detached house off-market for $4.5 million, adding to their property holdings in the Sydney suburb.Nathan Lyon and David Warner’s property movesOther Australian cricketers have also made moves in the property market. Pat Cummins’ Test teammate Nathan Lyon and his wife Emma recently sold their Tennyson Point home after just 21 days on the market, a week before its scheduled October auction. The property had carried a price guide of $4 million.Former Australian teammate David Warner and his wife Candice, meanwhile, are preparing to take their Maroubra investment apartment to auction on November 24. The couple purchased the two-bedroom property in 2017 for $975,000, and it is now being marketed with a guide of $1.2 million to $1.32 million.The refreshed apartment features ocean views towards Malabar Headland and a lock-up garage. It had reportedly been earning around $900 a week in rental income.Pat Cummins’ captaincy in focusCummins’ leadership of the Australian team has also come under scrutiny following comments attributed to former Australia batter Usman Khawaja about the 2018 Sandpaper ball-tampering scandal. Khawaja reportedly claimed that the wider Australian team was involved in the episode, bringing renewed attention to the controversy and the team’s response at the time.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
